note: Owned by the spec, not by the implementation. Tests assert the 10/10 split and that the ten invalid cases cover ten distinct diagnostic codes.

examples.why: Baseline: f64 arithmetic, division, early return. The smallest program the VM must run.
Two sequential early returns; exercises all-path return analysis.
The motivating example: while loop with a constant bound, float comparison, integer counter. Verifier must infer 8 iterations.
Array indexing inside a provably bounded loop. The induction variable must be linked to the array length for the bounds proof.
Loop starts at 1 after seeding with a[0]; tests that the verifier does not assume i starts at zero.
Pure integer arithmetic including truncating division; no overflow provable at compile time, so runtime trap applies.
Nested bounded loops: the gas bound is 6 x 6 blocks, so the verifier must multiply, not add, iteration bounds.
Explicit i64 -> f64 cast; there are no implicit numeric conversions in the language.
Only correctly-rounded builtins are allowed in the core; sqrt is IEEE-exact and therefore deterministic across engines.
Array literal, builtin call inside a loop, accumulator. End-to-end shape of a real generated program.
Loop body never changes the induction variable, so no iteration bound can be proven. Must be rejected before execution, not killed by a timer.
Direct recursion is rejected by default in v0.1: no decreasing-measure proof exists yet, and an unbounded stack breaks both memory and gas bounds.
Constant index 10 into a [f64; 8] is statically out of bounds; the verifier needs no SMT solver to reject it.
i32 + f64 does not typecheck; an explicit cast is required, which keeps lowering deterministic.
Only one branch returns; the fall-through path has no value. Every path must return, so the VM never falls off a function.
let is block-scoped; using x after the if-block closes is a name resolution error, not an uninitialized read.
Constant division by zero is rejected at compile time; the runtime trap covers the dynamic case.
add takes two arguments; calls never fill in defaults, so arity must match exactly.
The repeat literal [0.0; 5] has length 5 but the annotation says 4; array lengths are part of the type.
Indices must be integers; rejecting f64 indices removes a whole class of conversion ambiguity from the bounds analysis.
